title: Headers and include guards
goal: Trace two paths to a shared header, keep both includes, and define the type once per translation unit.

prerequisites.text: Recall structures and their members. The error arises because two include paths produce the same complete structure text.
Recall what #include and #define do during a build. That will help you see the limits of the guard.

terms.title: Direct inclusion
terms.definition: main.c explicitly names the header in its own #include directive.

terms.title: Nested inclusion
terms.definition: One header includes another. For example, gauge_scale.h includes gauge.h.

terms.title: Include guard
terms.definition: A #ifndef and #define pair using a unique name around a header body. A later visit sees the macro already defined and skips the body.

sections.title: The working model
paragraphs: The gauge project uses the Gauge type directly in its main file. The scale header is needed too and also includes gauge.h. Both paths are natural because each file declares its own dependencies.

At first, #ifndef GAUGE_H finds no definition. #define marks the first visit. When the scale includes gauge.h again, the condition is false and a second copy of the structure does not enter the C source.

The marker applies while processing one source file. A separately compiled .c starts its own preprocessing. A guard does not make it safe to put ordinary external function definitions in a header included from several .c files.

sections.title: Build a gauge with two paths to gauge.h
paragraphs: main.c includes gauge.h directly and also reaches it through gauge_scale.h. Predict how many definitions of struct Gauge remain in this translation unit.
steps: The direct include defines GAUGE_H and passes through the structure definition.
The include from gauge_scale.h reaches gauge.h again. The marker exists already, so the body is skipped.
The scale header still defines DEFAULT_GAUGE_MM as 18. main creates one Gauge record and prints the field.

sections.title: Identify the failed build stage
paragraphs: The message redefinition of 'Kit' means a complete structure reached the compiler twice. Trace both paths from main.c to kit.h and inspect the #ifndef, #define and #endif boundaries.
Removing an include can hide the fault while leaving kit.h fragile. Give it its own KIT_H guard and retain the direct dependency.
A guard is evaluated while each translation unit is preprocessed. Two separate .c files can include the same header and see its interface independently.

sections.title: Predict, verify, and explain
paragraphs: In a copy of the example, remove the guard from gauge.h. Predict the redefinition and locate the two include paths. Restore the guard, then swap the order of the two includes in main.c. Explain what remains the same.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Source inclusion, conditional directives, and structure tag declarations.

selfcheck.prompt: gauge.h has already been included when the preprocessor reaches gauge_scale.h. What happens on its next visit to gauge.h?
options: The linker combines two structures later
feedback: GAUGE_H prevents another pass through the body.
This happens during preprocessing, before linking.

selfcheck.prompt: Why should two distinct headers use different guard names?
options: The first could otherwise disable the second header body
The name sets a structure member value
Only the linker uses the guard name
feedback: With the same macro, the second #ifndef would be false.
A guard records a visit. Instance data comes from the initializer.

selfcheck.prompt: A rebuild works after deleting the direct #include "kit.h". Why is it better to keep the include and fix kit.h?
selfcheck.feedback: main.c uses the structure directly. A guard lets both main.c and kit_label.h include kit.h safely, so that dependency survives changes in the nested include path.

practice.title: Guard the kit record
practice.task: Add a direct include of kit.h to main.c and keep kit_label.h. Protect all of struct Kit with KIT_H. Print parts= and the number of parts at four per kit. The first line of stdin is one digit followed by LF or end of input. Otherwise print invalid and exit with code 1.
criteria: Both includes are present. kit.h has its own guard. Inputs 2, 0 and 9 yield parts=8, parts=0 and parts=36 respectively.
Two digits or an empty line yield invalid and exit code 1. stderr is empty for all run cases.
practice.hint: KIT_H must cover the body of kit.h itself. KIT_LABEL_H belongs to a different header and does not protect the direct path to kit.h.

steps.why: The only path to kit.h initially goes through kit_label.h.
Two paths now insert the unguarded struct Kit.

steps.action: Add the kit.h guard and the parts= prefix.
steps.why: Both paths remain, and the definition passes through once.

exercises.title: Reverse the include order
exercises.task: In a copy of your solution put kit_label.h before kit.h in main.c and run with 2 again. Point out where KIT_H is first defined now.
criteria: The rebuild and parts=8 still work. Explain why the first visit now comes from kit_label.h.

teaching.scene: A gauge module reaches its measurement structure through two include paths. Find both paths and arrange for one definition in each translation unit.

predict.prompt: main.c includes gauge.h and gauge_scale.h, which also includes gauge.h. How many definitions of struct Gauge does the compiler see in main, and what does the program print?
predict.answer: The first inclusion defines GAUGE_H and emits the structure definition. The second sees the macro and skips the body. main has one definition, and the program prints gauge=18 mm.

apply.prompt: In a copy of gauge.h, change the guard name in #define but leave the name in #ifndef unchanged. Predict the stage at which the failure appears.
apply.answer: The original name is never defined, so both paths see a true condition. Compiling main.c rejects the duplicate definition of struct Gauge. There is no program stdout.

practice.strategy: Draw both edges from main.c to kit.h: one direct and one through kit_label.h. Guard the structure in its own file, then keep both edges and verify the calculation for two kits.
practice.diagnosis: If the build works only after deleting the direct #include, you hid one route to the duplicate. Restore both routes and compare the macro names and the boundaries of the guard.

syntax.explanation: The guard macro starts out undefined, so the first inclusion processes the body. A repeat inclusion in the same translation unit finds that the macro is defined.
syntax.mistake: Sharing one guard name between two different headers can suppress declarations you need. Give each header a unique guard.
